## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven (rating 3 of 4 for boats).** Muskegon is a close second (3). South Haven (2) and St. Joseph (2) are weaker.
- **Grand Haven:** fish 100-160 ft of water, with lines around 50-90 ft down.
- **Lures:** glow plugs, glow spoons, meat rigs, and green rotator/fly combinations.
- **Check the wind forecast before you go.** I could not get a live forecast, so I can't judge the lake for this week.

## Why
- Grand Haven and Muskegon both had the best boat reports on the latest bulletin, rated good with the fish 50-100 ft down in 100-160 ft of water.
- South Haven and St. Joseph were rated slow or average in the weeks before, and only South Haven's Chinook recovered to good on July 30.
- I'd expect the Grand Haven and Muskegon fish to stay in the same depth range this week, since the buoy temperatures at both are similar.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (latest bulletin July 30, six days old):**
- Grand Haven, boat, quality 3: "Boat anglers found good numbers of salmon in 100 to 160 feet of water… Glow plugs, meat rigs, and rotator/fly combinations worked best 50 to 90 feet down." (Grand Haven, 2025-07-30)
- Muskegon, boat, quality 3: "The best action was 60 to 100 feet down in 100 to 160 feet of water… glow plugs, glow spoons, green rotator/fly combinations, and meat rigs all worked well." (Muskegon, 2025-07-30)
- South Haven, boat, quality 3 for Chinook and 1 for coho: "most successful fishing occurred around 95 feet of water… predominantly on spoons, while some of the larger salmon were caught using meat rigs." (South Haven, 2025-07-30)
- St. Joseph, boat, quality 2: "targeted waters from 90 to well beyond 110 feet… Rotators tipped with flies or meat rigs." (St. Joseph, 2025-07-30)
- The week before (July 23) was slow at South Haven and St. Joseph (quality 0). Grand Haven and Muskegon were already good that week (quality 3 and 2). (2025-07-23)

**Past seasons (history, not current):**
- Similar water temperatures in mid-August 2023 and late July 2024 gave good boat catches at Muskegon and Grand Haven (quality 3), with fish 30-90 ft down. (Muskegon, 2024-07-31; Grand Haven, 2023-08-16)
- A similar week in 2022 was only fair at Grand Haven and Muskegon, with scattered fish. (Grand Haven, 2022-08-17)

**Conditions:**
- The conditions tool returned a summary for the week before Aug 5, not live data. Buoy surface temperatures that week were about 67 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy 45161), 65 F at South Haven, and 69 F at St. Joseph. (Conditions, week of late July)
- Upwelling-favoring wind (north to east, 8+ mph) was about 9-10 hours in the last 3 days at Grand Haven and Muskegon. (Grand Haven, 2025-07-30; Muskegon, 2025-07-30)

## Caveats
- The newest bulletin is six days old. Recent fishing may have changed, and the July 30 report is my main basis.
- Conditions data is a summary for the prior week, not live. I have no current wind forecast, so I can't say whether small-boat conditions are safe this week.
- The buoy temperatures are measured, and the cold-layer depth isn't available here, so I can't give a modeled depth.
- The Grand Haven and Muskegon ratings come from the same buoy and similar reports, so they are close calls. Choose by launch and wind.
